basis: Cardiomyopathy, woolly hair and palmoplantar keratoderma define this cardioectodermal syndrome.
Familial enlargement of distal finger and toe phalanges is a skeletal disorder.
Craniofrontonasal malformation supports skeletal involvement; no definition or phenotypes establish additional axes.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the disorder; other functional organ abnormalities occur below 30%.
Tumor originates in the endocrine pancreas, including functional and nonfunctional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors.
Lissencephaly and cerebellar hypoplasia affect the brain; the defining cleft palate affects the oral cavity.
Chronic eczema/cutaneous inflammation is characteristic; colitis in 1/3. Cap prioritizes skin and bowel over vascular, lung, ocular and CNS inflammation.
Neurodevelopmental impairment, motor dysfunction and hearing loss define the syndrome; hypotonia does not establish primary muscle disease.
Usually arises in craniofacial bones, especially the maxilla; neuroectodermal lineage does not establish nervous-system involvement.
Immune-mediated cutaneous lichen planus produces persistent atrophic skin plaques.
Developmental impairment, parkinsonism and peripheral neuropathy define neurological disease; amyotrophy and dysphagia reflect neurological dysfunction.
Tumor originates in the vagina, a reproductive organ outside the available axes.
Primary muscular dystrophy with joint contractures and hyperlaxity; respiratory failure and intellectual impairment are explicitly rare.
FG syndrome is defined by neurodevelopmental impairment and hypotonia; constipation alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Hypogammaglobulinemic immunodeficiency; multicystic kidney dysplasia in 2/5 (40%). Macrocytosis alone does not establish blood-cell damage.
Intellectual disability and autism define the disorder; myopia affects vision in 2/4 (50%). High palate alone does not establish oral dysfunction.
Ovarian endocrine failure causes low estradiol and elevated FSH; short stature and delayed skeletal maturation do not establish skeletal damage.
Defining ectodermal defects affect sweat glands, hair and skin, with dental agenesis and abnormal dentition in 80–99%.
Polyp located in the colon; the umbrella includes several histologic subtypes without a shared immune mechanism.
Middle-ear effusion impairs hearing; serous otitis does not necessarily represent an infection or immune-mediated disease.
Anemia caused by defective enzyme activity, represented by erythrocyte metabolic enzyme disorders.
Folate-responsive megaloblastic anemia with abnormal folate metabolism; the stated folate-transporter-deficiency parent includes immunodeficiency.
Neonatal diabetes, developmental delay and epilepsy define DEND; weakness and hypotonia do not independently establish muscle damage.
Hyperplasia is confined to the uterine endometrium, a reproductive tissue outside the available axes.
Inherited retinal dystrophy causes congenital blindness; no extraocular disease is established.
